meta.title: Water-in-Salt Zinc Electrolyte Atlas
meta.subtitle: An interactive research microsite built around the ICEMEE 2026 manuscript on organic co-solvents for WIS zinc-ion battery electrolytes.
meta.author: Xueyang Song

narrative.whyItMatters: Aqueous zinc batteries promise lower cost and higher intrinsic safety than lithium-ion systems, but water activity, hydrogen evolution, and plating instability still limit practical deployment.
narrative.wisFrame: Water-in-salt and co-solvent-rich electrolytes reshape Zn2+ solvation, suppress water reactivity, and can trade off stability against conductivity in ways that are difficult to compare across papers without a shared dataset.
narrative.honestLimit: Only lifespan and ionic conductivity produced useful cross-study signal. CE and ESW remain important experimentally, but the literature still reports them too unevenly for robust transfer learning.

lifespan.note: Competitive but less stable than RF.
Linear baseline underfits the cross-study data.

conductivity.note: Reasonable but less sharp than XGBoost.
Too rigid for the mixed-literature feature space.

ce.note: CE reporting was too inconsistent to generalize.

esw.note: Electrochemical stability windows were too unevenly reported.
Still below the mean-baseline despite flexible kernels.

paretoCandidates.name: DMSO
paretoCandidates.note: Strong donor and repeatedly favorable across the curated set.

paretoCandidates.name: DMF
paretoCandidates.note: Maintains conductivity better than heavier glycol-rich systems.

paretoCandidates.name: TEP
paretoCandidates.note: High boiling point and repeated Pareto presence support follow-up testing.

paretoCandidates.name: NMP
paretoCandidates.note: Interesting chemical neighborhood match, but still outside the training manifold.

paretoCandidates.name: Sulfolane
paretoCandidates.note: Excellent thermal safety, but mobility penalties remain visible.

paretoCandidates.name: Ethylene glycol
paretoCandidates.note: Frequent in the dataset and useful as a benchmark co-solvent.

recommendations.title: Start with DMSO as the internal check
recommendations.body: It is already present in the curated literature and lands inside the favorable Pareto region with strong donor character.

recommendations.title: Use DMF when conductivity needs to stay high
recommendations.body: Its lower viscosity preserves transport better than many heavier donor-rich solvents.

recommendations.title: Carry TEP when safety and boiling point matter
recommendations.body: TEP trades some conductivity for a safer thermal profile and still remains competitively ranked.

recommendations.title: Treat NMP as a hypothesis, not a result
recommendations.body: NMP sits in an attractive descriptor neighborhood but remains extrapolative relative to the training corpus.
